answer: According to arXiv 2503.18983, the right to life under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) expressly protects individuals from "arbitrary" deprivations of life. The term 'arbitrary' deprivation means that an interference with the right to life should not be arbitrary; it must be prescribed by law, proportionate to the ends sought, and necessary in the circumstances of the case considering the availability of less harmful means. An arbitrary deprivation of life is defined as involving an interference that is (1) not prescribed by law, (2) disproportionate to the ends sought, and (3) not necessary in the circumstances of the case.
